ex.ja: 非喫煙者は新しい禁煙法を支持して結集しています。

ex.en: The Tokyo Stock Exchange rallied at the end of the day.
ex.ja: 東京証券取引所は後場の終わり値になって持ち直しました。

ex.en: When is the pep rally?
ex.ja: 壮行式は何時からですか。

en: That which represents something else.
The act of representing.

representation.ety: From Late Middle English representacioun, from Old French representacion, from Latin repraesentātiō. By surface analysis, represent + -ation.

ex.en: This painting is a representation of a storm at sea.
ex.ja: この絵は海の嵐を描いたものである。

note.ja: re（再び）+ pre（前に）+ sent（ある）+ ation。再び目の前に示すこと →「表現・代表」。represent（表す・代表する）。

en: A quantity obtained by addition or aggregation.
An arithmetic computation, especially one posed to a student as an exercise (not necessarily limited to addition).
To add together.
To give a summary of.

sum.ety: From Middle English summe, from Old French summe, from Latin summa (“highest point; sum”), from summus (“highest”).

ex.en: He received a large sum in insurance benefit.
ex.ja: 彼は保険金として大金を受け取った。

ex.en: She had only a small sum of money.
ex.ja: 彼女は小額の金しか持っていなかった。

ex.en: The plan requires a large sum of money.
ex.ja: その計画にはたくさんのお金が必要だ。

note.ja: ラテン語 summa（最も上の・総計）から。一番上に書かれた合計 →「合計・金額」。

en: To rotate about an off-centre fixed point.
To dance.
The act, or an instance, of swinging.
The manner in which something is swung.

swing.ety: From Middle English swyngen, from Old English swingan, from Proto-West Germanic *swingan, from Proto-Germanic *swinganą (compare Low German swingen, German schwingen, Dutch zwingen, Swedish svinga), from Proto-Indo-European *swenk-, *sweng- (compare Scottish Gaelic seang (“thin”)). Related to swink.

ex.ja: トムがブランコから落ちて怪我しちゃったんだよ。

ex.en: The swing is moving up and down.
ex.ja: ぶらんこが上下に動いている。

ex.en: They like to play on the swings in the park.
ex.ja: あの子たち、公園のブランコで遊ぶのが好きなのよ。

To swing with the stern in a certain direction; said of a vessel at anchor.
Limited; abridged; reduced; curtailed.

ex.en: I can't make head nor tail of it.
ex.ja: 私はそれを理解できない。

Either of two similar or closely related objects, plans, institutions, people, etc.
To separate, divide.
To split, part; to go away, depart.
Double; dual; occurring as a matching pair.
Forming a pair of twins.

en: A person with long experience of a particular activity.
A person who has served in the armed forces, especially an old soldier who has seen long service.
Having had long experience, practice, or service.
Of or relating to former members of the military armed forces, especially those who served during wartime.

veteran.ety: Borrowed from Middle French vétéran, from Latin veterānus.

ex.ja: 私の叔父はベトナム戦争の退役軍人だ。

en: Attentive; awake; on guard.
An alarm.
A notification of higher importance than an advisory.
To give warning to.

alert.ety: From French alerte (“alert”), from the phrase à l'erte (“on the watch”), from Italian all'erta (“to the height”), from erta (“lookout, tower”).

ex.en: Be alert when you cross a busy street!
ex.ja: 車の多い通りの横断には油断するな！

ex.en: The hunter was alert to every sound and movement.
ex.ja: 狩猟者はあらゆる動きに気をくばっていた。

ex.en: He is alert to every chance of making money.
ex.ja: 彼は金もうけのあらゆる機会に目ざとい。

arena.ety: Borrowed from Latin arēna (“sand; arena”), from earlier harēna, from Old Latin hasēna, possibly from Etruscan; compare Sabine fasēna.

en: To make a loud, hollow, resonant sound.
To exclaim with force, to shout, to thunder.
A low-pitched, resonant sound, such as of an explosion.
A rapid expansion or increase.
Used to suggest the sound of an explosion.
Used to suggest something happening suddenly or unexpectedly; voilà.

boom.ety: Onomatopoeic, perhaps borrowed; compare German bummen, Dutch bommen (“to hum, buzz”). The sense "a period of economic growth" is generally taken to derive from the sense "a rapid expansion", although other origins have also been suggested.

ex.en: All the industries in the city are booming.
ex.ja: 市の産業はみんな好景気に沸いている。

ex.en: The computer industry is enjoying a boom.
ex.ja: コンピューター業界は景気がいい。

ex.en: We have been visited by a nation-wide economic boom.
ex.ja: 全国的に好景気に見舞われている。

en: A heavy shoe that covers part of the leg.
A kind of sports shoe worn by players of certain games such as cricket and football (historically in the form of boots, now shorter, but …
To kick.
To put boots on, especially for riding.

boot.ety: From Middle English boote, bote (“shoe”), from Old French bote (“a high, thick shoe”). Of obscure origin, but probably related to Old French bot (“club-foot”), bot (“fat, short, blunt”), from Old Frankish *butt, from Proto-Germanic *buttaz, *butaz (“cut off, short, numb, blunt”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰewt-, *bʰewd- (“to strike, push, shock”); if so, a doublet of butt. Compare Old Norse butt (“stump”), Low German butt (“blunt, plump”), Old English bytt (“small piece of land”), buttuc (“end”). More at buttock and debut.

ex.en: I would like to purchase some boots.
ex.ja: ブーツを買いたいんですけど。

ex.en: A group of people started off in snow boots.
ex.ja: 人々の一団はスノーブーツを履いて出発した。

ex.en: Her boots wear out much more quickly than mine.
ex.ja: 彼女のブーツは私のものよりずっと早くだめになる。

en: Strong in the face of fear; courageous.
Making a fine show or display.
To encounter or withstand with courage and fortitude, to defy, to provoke.

brave.ety: From Middle French brave, borrowed from Italian bravo, itself of uncertain origin (see there). Doublet of bravo.

ex.en: He appears brave, but it's just an act.
ex.ja: 彼は勇敢そうに見えるけど見せかけだけだ。

ex.en: The officer inspired his men to be brave.
ex.ja: 将校は部下を鼓舞して勇気を出させた。

ex.en: He was brave enough to go there alone.
ex.ja: 彼は勇敢にも一人でそこへ行った。

en: A solid upright structure designed usually to support a larger structure above it, such as a roof or horizontal beam, but sometimes for d…
A vertical line of entries in a table, usually read from top to bottom.

From Middle English columne, columpne, columpe, borrowed from Old French columne, from Latin columna (“a column, pillar, post”), originally a collateral form of columen, contraction culmen (“a pillar, top, crown, summit”). Akin to Latin collis (“a hill”), celsus (“high”), probably to Ancient Greek κολοφών (kolophṓn, “top, summit”). Displaced native Old English sweor (“pillar, column”) and Old English stapol.

ex.en: I'm always interested in reading his column.
ex.ja: 私はいつも彼のコラムを興味をもって読む。

ex.ja: 私はいつも彼のコラムを興味をもって読む。

ex.en: Add up this column of figures.
ex.ja: この数字の列を合計しなさい。

en: The act or principle of compensating.
Something which is regarded as an equivalent; something which compensates for loss.

compensation.ety: From Middle English compensacioun, from Old French compensacion, from Latin compensātiōnem, accusative singular of compensātiō. Equivalent to compensate + -ion.

ex.en: The victims are entitled to compensation for their injuries.
ex.ja: 被害者たちにはけがの補償を受ける権利がある。

ex.en: I promise you every possible compensation.
ex.ja: できる限りの償いはするつもりだ。

ex.en: The compensation will be huge.
ex.ja: 賠償金えぐいことになるな。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pens（量る）+ ation。釣り合うように量ること →「補償・報酬」。

en: The act of putting together; assembly.
A mixture or compound; the result of composing.

composition.ety: From Middle English composicioun, borrowed from Old French composicion, from Latin compositiō, compositiōnem.

ex.en: His composition is not perfectly free of mistakes.
ex.ja: 彼の作文は完全に誤りがないというわけではない。

ex.en: I had my teacher correct my English composition.
ex.ja: 私は先生に英作文を直してもらった。

ex.en: The English of this composition is too good.
ex.ja: この英作文はよくできすぎている。

note.ja: com（共に）+ pos（置く）+ ition。一緒に置いて組み立てること →「構成・作文・作曲」。

en: The act of preserving, guarding, or protecting; the keeping (of a thing) in a safe or entire state; preservation.
Wise use of natural resources.

conservation.ety: From Old French. By surface analysis, conserve + -ation.

ex.en: Forest conservation is an important issue all over the world.
ex.ja: 森林の保護は世界中の重要な問題だ。

ex.en: This has been designated a conservation area.
ex.ja: この地域は保全地域に指定されています。

ex.en: The organization plays a principal role in wildlife conservation.
ex.ja: その団体は野生動物の保護において、最も重要な役割を果たしている。

en: A measure of the mass of matter contained by a unit volume.
The ratio of one quantity, representing something of interest, to another quantity representing space, area, or extent in which the thing…

density.ety: Borrowed from Middle French densité or Latin densitas. Morphologically dense + -ity.

ex.en: Japan has a high population density.
ex.ja: 日本は人口密度が高い国である。

ex.en: What's the country with the highest population density in the world?
ex.ja: 世界で一番人口が密集している国はどこですか？

ex.en: A recent survey revealed that the population density in the metropolis was decreasing.
ex.ja: 最近の調査は大都市の人口密度がていかしていることを示した。

en: The state of being difficult, or hard to do.
An obstacle that hinders achievement of a goal.

difficulty.ety: From Middle English difficulte, from Middle French and Anglo-Norman difficulte and their etymon Latin difficultas, from difficul, older form of difficilis (“hard to do, difficult”), from dis- + facilis (“easy”); see difficile and difficult. Equivalent to dis- + facile + -ty. Also analysable as difficult + -y, though the adjective is historically a backformation from the noun.

ex.en: I had no difficulty in finding his office.
ex.ja: 簡単に彼の事務所が見付かった。

ex.en: He had no difficulty in finding the place.
ex.ja: 彼は難なくその場所を見つけた。

ex.en: Come to me if you are in difficulties.
ex.ja: 困ったら私のところへきたまえ。

note.ja: dif（否定）+ fic（する）+ ult + y。容易にできないこと →「困難」。

en: Relating to the basic, essential or fundamental part of something.
Very simple.
A supernatural being associated with the elements.

elementary.ety: From Middle English elementare, from Latin elementārius (“elementary”), from elementum (“one of the four elements of antiquity; fundamentals”) + -ārius (adjective-forming suffix). Cognate with French élémentaire. By surface analysis, element + -ary.

ex.en: He is in fourth grade of elementary school.
ex.ja: 彼は小学４年生です。

ex.en: There used to be an elementary school here.
ex.ja: ここにもとは小学校があった。

ex.en: My little brother goes to an elementary school.
ex.ja: 弟は小学校へ通っています。

The elimination or consumption of something, sometimes with the notion of loss or damage to the thing eliminated.
To charge a cost against an expense account; to bill something to the company for which one works.

expense.ety: From Middle English expense, from Anglo-Norman expense and Old French espense, from Late Latin expēnsa, from Latin expendō. See expend. Doublet of speso.

ex.en: I had a good dinner at his expense.
ex.ja: 彼に払ってもらっておいしい食事をした。

ex.ja: 彼女は自分の負担で本を出版した。

ex.en: We cannot avoid cutting down our living expenses.
ex.ja: 私達は生活費を切り詰めざるを得ない。

Swift in motion; light and quick in going from place to place.
Light; superficially thin; not penetrating deep, as soil.

ex.ja: 少年老い易く学成り難し。

Extraordinary mental capacity.
Ingenious, brilliant, very clever, or original.

genius.ety: From Latin genius (“inborn nature; a tutelary deity of a person or place; wit, brilliance”), from gignō (“to beget, produce”), Old Latin genō, from the Proto-Indo-European root *ǵenh₁-. Doublet of genio. See also genus and genie.

ex.ja: 彼女は天才だと信じられている。

ex.en: He is what we call a musical genius.
ex.ja: 彼はいわゆる音楽的天才である。

ex.en: I found him a genius at chemistry.
ex.ja: 彼が化学の天才であることに気づいた。

greatly.ety: Inherited from Middle English gretly. By surface analysis, great + -ly.

ex.en: He is the greatest man in the world.
ex.ja: 彼は世界中で一番偉大な人です。

ex.ja: 僕、無芸大食で何の取り柄もないんです。

en: The act or process of infecting.

ex.ja: 感染の広がりはとても危ないです。

ex.ja: 中耳炎になったことはありますか？

ex.en: He showed courage in the face of danger.
ex.ja: 彼は危険をかえりみず勇気を示した。

ex.en: Your courage will come out in a crisis.
ex.ja: いざとなれば勇気が湧いてくる。

note.ja: ラテン語 cor（心）から。cour + age。心の力 →「勇気」。

en: A method, device or medication that restores good health.
An act of healing or state of being healed; restoration to health after a disease, or to soundness after injury.
To restore to health.
To bring (a disease or its bad effects) to an end.

cure.ety: From Middle English cure, borrowed from Old French cure (“care, cure, healing, cure of souls”), from Latin cura (“care, medical attendance, cure”). Displaced native Old English hǣlu, but this survived as heal.

ex.en: Scientists haven't found a cure for cancer yet.
ex.ja: 科学者たちは未だに癌を完治させる方法を見出していない。

ex.en: This medicine will cure you of that disease.
ex.ja: この薬を飲めばその病気は治るでしょう。

ex.en: Cancer can be cured if discovered in time.
ex.ja: 発見が間に合えば、ガンは治療できる。

note.ja: ラテン語 cura（世話）から。世話をする →「治す・治療」。

en: In dire need (of something); having a dire need or desire.
Being filled with, or in a state of, despair; hopeless.
A person in desperate circumstances or who is at the point of desperation, such as a down-and-outer, addict, etc.

desperate.ety: From Middle English desperat(e) (“desperate”), borrowed from Latin dēspērātus, perfect passive participle of dēspērō (“to be without hope”), see -ate (adjective-forming suffix). The noun is derived from the adjective or from the Latin source through substantivization, see -ate (noun-forming suffix).

ex.en: He is in desperate search of further evidence.
ex.ja: 彼はもっと証拠がないかと、やっきになって捜している。

ex.en: He was desperate to defend his reputation.
ex.ja: 彼は名声を守ろうと必死だった。

ex.en: Tom was desperate to defend his reputation.
ex.ja: トムは自分の評判を守るのに必死だった。

en: The quality of being diverse or different; a difference or unlikeness.
A variety; diverse types or examples.

diversity.ety: From Middle English diversite, from Old French diversité, from Latin dīversitās, equivalent to diverse + -ity. Displaced native Old English mislīcnes.

ex.en: This forest is full of diversity.
ex.ja: この森は、多様性に富んでいます。

ex.en: Existing legislation does not take diversity of races into account.
ex.ja: 現行の法律は人種の多様性を考慮していない。

note.ja: di（離れて）+ vers（向ける）+ ity。別々の方向を向いていること →「多様性」。

en: The day or night before, usually used for holidays, such as Christmas Eve.
The period of time when something is just about to happen or to be introduced

eve.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₁ep-der.
Proto-Indo-European *h₁épsder.
Proto-Indo-European *h₁épider.
Proto-Germanic *ēbanþs
Proto-West Germanic *ābanþ
Old English ǣfen
Middle English evender.
Middle English eve
English eve
Inherited from Middle English eve, variant of even (itself from Old English ǣfen), with a pre-1200 loss of the terminal '-n'. See also the now archaic or poetic even (“evening”), from the same source.
In medieval Europe, days were considered to extend from sunset to sunset rather than midnight to midnight, so the night before a holiday was considered part of it, hence

ex.en: It is Eve that sets Adam on.
ex.ja: アダムをそそのかしたのはイブだ。

ex.en: Tom wanted to spend New Year's Eve with Mary.
ex.ja: トムはメアリーと一緒に大晦日を過ごしたかった。

ex.en: That time was before New Year's Eve.
ex.ja: あの時は大晦日前だった。

en: The academic staff at schools, colleges, universities or not-for-profit research institutes, as opposed to the students or support staff.
A division of a university.

faculty.ety: From Middle English faculte (“power, property”), from Old French faculte, from Latin facultas (“capability, ability, skill, abundance, plenty, stock, goods, property; in Medieval Latin also a body of teachers”), another form of facilitas (“easiness, facility, etc.”), from facul, another form of facilis (“easy, facile”); see facile. Doublet of facility.

ex.en: He has the faculty to learn languages easily.
ex.ja: 彼は言葉を簡単に学ぶ能力をもっている。

ex.en: He has a faculty for making other people happy.
ex.ja: 彼は他人を楽しくさせる才能を持っている。

ex.en: She has a great faculty for music.
ex.ja: 彼女は音楽に優れた才能がある。

note.ja: ラテン語 facultas（できること）から。fac（する）。物事をする力 →「能力・機能」、（大学の）学部・教員。

en: Critical assessment of a process or activity or of their results.
The part of an output signal that is looped back into the input to control or modify a system.
To generate the high-frequency sound by allowing a speaker to cause vibration of the sound generator of a musical instrument connected by…
To provide informational feedback to.

feedback.ety:
Etymology tree
English feed
Proto-Indo-European *bʰeg-der.?
Proto-Germanic *baką
Proto-West Germanic *bak
Old English bæc
Middle English bak
English back
English feedback
From feed + back.

ex.en: Thank you for your valuable feedback.
ex.ja: 貴重なご意見をありがとうございます。

ex.en: We look forward to your feedback.
ex.ja: 僕らは君のフィードバックを楽しみしています。

ex.en: Please review the contents and provide any appropriate feedback.
ex.ja: 内容をご覧になり、適切なご意見をいただければ幸いです。

en: A person who fights; a combatant.
A warrior; a fighting soldier.

fighter.ety: From Middle English fightere, feghtere, from Old English feohtere. Equivalent to fight + -er.

ex.en: The fire fighters put out the fire.
ex.ja: 消防士は火事を消した。

ex.en: You're still a fire fighter, aren't you?
ex.ja: 今でも消防士なんでしょ？

ex.en: That fighter plane dropped a bomb.
ex.ja: その戦闘機は爆弾を投下した。

en: Especially of a liquid, to become solid due to low temperature.
To lower something's temperature to the point that it freezes or becomes hard.
A period of intensely cold weather.
A halt of a regular operation.

freeze.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *prews-der.
Proto-Germanic *-āną
Proto-Germanic *freusaną
Proto-West Germanic *freusan
Old English frēosan
Middle English fresen
English freeze
From Middle English fresen, from Old English frēosan (“to freeze”), from Proto-West Germanic *freusan, from Proto-Germanic *freusaną (“to freeze”), from Proto-Indo-European *prews- (“to freeze; frost”).
Cognates
Cognate with North Frisian friis, friise, früüs (“to freeze”), Saterland Frisian fjoose, frjoze (“to freeze”), West Frisian frieze (“to freeze”), Central Franconian freese (“to freeze”), Cimbrian briizan, vrii

ex.en: How long can we keep this frozen food?
ex.ja: この冷凍食品はどのくらい保存できますか。

ex.en: What do you call it when water freezes?
ex.ja: 水が凍ったとき、それを何と呼びますか。

ex.en: She froze at the sight of the bear.
ex.ja: 彼女は熊を見かけて身がすくんだ。

en: Humankind; human beings as a group.
The human condition or nature.

humanity.ety: Inherited from Middle English humanyte, humanite, humanitye, from Old French humanité, from Latin hūmānitās. By surface analysis, human or humane + -ity. Partly displaced mankind, from Old English mancynn (literally “human race”).

ex.en: You should work in the interests of humanity.
ex.ja: 諸君は人類の利益のために働くべきだ。

ex.en: Nuclear weapons are a threat to all humanity.
ex.ja: 核兵器は全人類への脅威である。

ex.en: I'll do anything in the interests of humanity.
ex.ja: 人類のためになんでもするつもりだ。

en: The act of innovating; the introduction of something new, in customs, rites, etc.
A change effected by innovating; a change in customs.

innovation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French innovation, from Old French innovacion, from Late Latin innovatio, innovationem, from Latin innovo, innovatus. Morphologically innovate + -ion.

ex.en: A company that stifles innovation can't hope to grow very much.
ex.ja: 出る杭が打たれる会社じゃ、大きな成長は望めないね。

ex.en: Technological innovation brought about the rapid progress of the information industry.
ex.ja: 技術革新は情報産業に急速な進歩をもたらした。

ex.en: Open source is the engine that drives technological innovation.
ex.ja: オープンソースは技術革新をドライブするエンジンである。

en: A device used to produce music.
A means or agency for achieving an aspect.
To apply measuring devices.
To devise, conceive, cook up, plan.

instrument.ety:
From Middle English instrument, from Old French instrument, from Latin īnstrūmentum (“an implement, tool”),
From īnstruō (“build, construct; arrange”) + -mentum.

ex.en: You should on no condition touch these instruments.
ex.ja: どんなことがあってもこれらの器具に触れてはならない。

ex.en: You play a musical instrument, don't you?
ex.ja: あなたは楽器を演奏しますよね。

ex.en: Do you play a musical instrument?
ex.ja: 楽器をなにか演奏しますか。

note.ja: in（中に）+ stru（積む・備える）+ ment。備えておく道具 →「器具・楽器」。

en: To spend money, time, or energy on something, especially for some benefit or purpose; used with in.
To envelop, wrap, cover.
A designated area of disturbed weather that is being monitored for potential tropical cyclone development.

invest.ety: Borrowed from Middle French investir or Medieval Latin investire, from Latin investio (“to clothe, cover”), from in- (“in, on”) + vestio (“to clothe, dress”), from vestis (“clothing”); see vest. The sense “to spend money etc.” probably via Italian investire, of the same root.

ex.en: The government should invest more money in industry.
ex.ja: 政府は産業にもっと多くの金を投資すべきだ。

ex.en: The Prime Minister is invested with incredible powers.
ex.ja: 首相は信じられないほどの権力を与えられている。

ex.en: The government should invest more money in agriculture.
ex.ja: 政府は農業にもっと投資するべきだ。

en: A piece of clothing worn on the upper body outside a shirt or blouse, often waist length to thigh length.
A piece of a person's suit, beside trousers and, sometimes, waistcoat; coat (US).
To confine (someone) to a straitjacket.
To enclose or encase in a jacket or other covering.

jacket.ety: From Middle French jacquet, diminutive of Old French jaque.

ex.en: I want the same jacket as you're wearing.
ex.ja: 私はあなたが今着ているのと同じジャケットが欲しい。

ex.en: Do you have this jacket in different colors?
ex.ja: このジャケットの色違いはありますか。

ex.en: There was a black jacket on the book.
ex.ja: その本には黒いカバーがかかっていた。

en: Making, or having the power to make, a law or laws; lawmaking.
That branch of government which is responsible for making, or having the power to make, a law or laws.

legislative.ety:
Etymology tree
English legislate
Proto-Indo-European *-wós
Proto-Indo-European *-iHwósder.
Latin -īvus
Old French -ifbor.
Middle English -yf
English -ive
English legislative
From legislate + -ive.

en: Synonym of handbook.
A booklet that instructs on the usage of a particular machine or product.
Performed with the hands.
Operated by means of the hands.

manual.ety: From Middle English manuel, from Old French manuel, from Late Latin manuāle (“handbook, manual”).

ex.en: He did hard manual labor through the day.
ex.ja: 彼はその日ずっと、つらい手仕事をやった。

ex.en: Manual labor is necessary in this company.
ex.ja: この会社では肉体労働が必要です。

ex.en: Do you drive a manual or automatic?
ex.ja: マニュアルを運転するの？それともオートマ？

note.ja: man（手）+ ual。手の →「手動の・手作業の」、手元に置く本 →「説明書」。

en: To fill.
To possess or use the time or capacity of; to engage the service of.

occupy.ety: From Middle English occupien, occupyen, borrowed from Old French occuper, from Latin occupāre (“to take possession of, seize, occupy, take up, employ”), from ob (“to, on”) + capiō (“to take”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *kap- (“to seize, grab”). Doublet of occupate, now obsolete.

ex.en: The meeting room is occupied at the moment.
ex.ja: 会議室は現在使用中です。

ex.en: The city was soon occupied by the soldiers.
ex.ja: その市はやがて兵隊によって占領された。

ex.en: He was fully occupied with his writing.
ex.ja: 彼は著述に励んでいた。

en: A person or organisation that operates a device, system, service, etc.
A telecommunications facilitator whose job is to connect or otherwise assist callers.

operator.ety: Borrowed from Latin operātor, from operor (“work, labour”). Equivalent to operate + -or.

ex.en: The operator put me through to New York.
ex.ja: 交換手が電話をニューヨークへつないでくれた。

ex.en: Operator, I'm trying to get through to Boston.
ex.ja: 交換台、ボストンに電話しようとしているんですが。

ex.en: This is the operator. Which extension would you like?
ex.ja: 交換手です。内線番号をどうぞ。

en: Causing pain or distress, either physical or mental.
Afflicted or suffering with pain (of a body part or, formerly, of a person).

painful.ety: From Middle English paynful, peinful, peynful, paynefull, peynefull, equivalent to pain + -ful. Compare Danish pinefuld (“painful”).

ex.en: It's painful to keep sitting for hours.
ex.ja: 何時間も座っているのは苦痛だ。

ex.en: There's nothing more painful than losing one's loved child.
ex.ja: 愛する我が子を失うことほど辛いことはない。

ex.en: Sometimes, life is difficult and painful.
ex.ja: 時には人生が辛くて難しい。

en: The act of preparing or getting ready.
The state of being prepared; readiness.

preparation.ety: From Middle English preparacion, from Middle French preparacion, from Latin praeparatio, praeparationem. Morphologically prepare + -ation.

ex.en: In preparation, clean the bath and fill it.
ex.ja: お風呂洗って、入れといてね。

ex.en: We failed due to a lack of preparation.
ex.ja: 我々は準備不足で失敗した。

ex.en: Have you finished your preparations for the trip?
ex.ja: 旅行の準備はすべて終わりましたか。

en: A hit or strike with one's fist.
Power, strength, energy.
To strike with one's fist.
To herd (cattle) as a cowboy.

punch.ety: From Middle English punchen, partially from Old French ponchonner (“to punch”), from ponchon (“pointed tool”), from Latin punctio, from punctus, perfect passive participle of pungō (“I prick”); and partially from Middle English punchen, a syncopated variant of punischen ("to punish"; see punish). Also influenced by Middle English punchon ("a punch"; see puncheon). Compare also Middle English bunchen, bonchen (“to punch, deliver a blow, pound, beat”).

ex.en: Do you want another glass of fruit punch?
ex.ja: フルーツポンチをもういっぱい欲しい？

ex.en: Oh, no! I forgot to punch in again!
ex.ja: あらいやだ。また、タイムカードを押し忘れた。

ex.en: I want to punch you in the face.
ex.ja: お前の顔を殴りたい。

en: A colour between red and blue; violet, though often closer to magenta.
Any non-spectral colour on the line of purples on a colour chromaticity diagram or a colour wheel between violet and red.
Of a purple hue.
Not predominantly red or blue, but having a mixture of Democrat and Republican support.
To turn purple in colour.
To dye purple.

purple.ety:
From Middle English purple, purpel, from Old English purpul (“purple”, adjective), taken from Old English purpure (“purple colour”, noun), from Latin purpura (“purple dye, shellfish”), from Ancient Greek πορφύρα (porphúra, “purple-fish”), perhaps of Semitic origin. Doublet of purpura and purpure.
The sense of "imperial power" is from the wearing of the color purple by emperors and kings.

ex.en: The boy wearing the purple baseball cap is Tom.
ex.ja: 紫の野球帽をかぶっている子がトムよ。

ex.en: Red and blue paint mixed together give us purple.
ex.ja: 赤と青を混ぜると紫になる。

ex.en: If you mix blue and red, you'll get purple.
ex.ja: 青と赤を混ぜると紫になる。

en: A permanent track consisting of fixed metal rails to drive trains or similar motorized vehicles on.
The transportation system comprising such tracks and vehicles fitted to travel on the rails, usually with several vehicles connected toge…
To transport via railroad.
To operate a railroad.

ex.en: He works on the railroad as a driver.
ex.ja: 彼は運転士として鉄道で働いている。

ex.en: The railroad workers are going on strike tomorrow.
ex.ja: 明日は鉄道がストですよ。

ex.en: He was killed in a railroad accident.
ex.ja: 彼は鉄道事故で死んだ。

en: The act of signing up or registering for something.
That which registers or makes something official, e.g. the form or paper that registers.

registration.ety:
Etymology tree
English register
Proto-Indo-European *-tis
Proto-Indo-European *-Hō
Proto-Indo-European *-tiHō
Proto-Italic *-tiō
Latin -tiō
Latin -ātiōlbor.
Old French -ationbor.
Middle English -acioun
English -ation
English registration
From register + -ation.

ex.en: I forgot to bring my medical registration ticket.
ex.ja: 診察券を持って来るのを忘れてしまいました。

ex.en: YouTube registration requires a real name and an address.
ex.ja: YouTubeの登録には本名と住所が要ります。

ex.en: Registration for the first visit is at Counter No.1.
ex.ja: 初診の受付は一番窓口です。

zh: 浪漫的愛情 /浪漫的爱情

en: An intimate relationship between two people; a love affair.
A strong obsession or attachment for something or someone.
To woo; to court.
To write or tell romantic stories, poetry, letters, etc.

romance.ety: From Middle English romauns, roumance, borrowed from Anglo-Norman and Old French romanz, romans (the vernacular language of France, as opposed to Latin), from Medieval Latin rōmānicē, Vulgar Latin rōmānicē (“in the Roman language”, adverb), from Latin rōmānicus (“roman”, adjective) from rōmānus (“a Roman”). Doublet of Romansch.

ex.en: His romance was the talk of the town.
ex.ja: 浮き名を流したものだ。

ex.en: Can you recommend a romance novel for me?
ex.ja: おすすめの恋愛小説はありますか？

ex.en: To love oneself is the beginning of a life-long romance.
ex.ja: 自分を愛するというのは一生続くロマンスの始まりだ。

en: To yield or give way to another.
To yield (something) to another, as when defeated.

submit.ety: From Middle English submitten, borrowed from Latin submittere, infinitive of submittō (“place under, yield”), from sub (“under, from below, up”) + mitto (“to send”). Compare upsend.

ex.en: I was forced to submit to my fate.
ex.ja: 私は運命に服従せざるを得なかった。

ex.en: He had to submit himself to their decision.
ex.ja: 彼は彼らの決定に従うほかなかった。

ex.en: He is the last man to submit to authority.
ex.ja: 彼はなかなか権威に屈するような男ではない。

note.ja: sub（下に）+ mit（送る）。下に差し出す →「提出する・服従する」。

en: An adequate quantity of; enough.
A quantity (of something) that is as large as is needed.
Of a type or kind that suffices, that satisfies requirements or needs.
Possessing adequate talents or accomplishments; of competent power or ability; qualified; fit.

sufficient.ety: From Old French sufisanz, soficient, from Latin sufficiēns, present participle of sufficiō.

ex.en: It's not particularly wonderful, but it is sufficient.
ex.ja: 取り立ててすばらしいわけではないが満足できる。

ex.en: He has a sufficient income to support his family.
ex.ja: 彼は家族を養うだけの収入がある。

ex.en: These are not sufficient reasons for breaking the promise.
ex.ja: これらは約束を破ったことの十分な理由にならない。

note.ja: suf（下から）+ fic（作る）+ ient。下から作り上げて満たす →「十分な」。

en: To halt something temporarily.
To hold in an undetermined or undecided state.

suspend.ety: From Old French sospendre, from Latin suspendere.

ex.en: Suspending the trial is out of the question.
ex.ja: 裁判を中断するのは不可能だ。

ex.en: The school principal suspended Tom for two days.
ex.ja: 学校長はトムを２日間の停学にした。

ex.en: Tom has been suspended from school for three weeks.
ex.ja: トムは３週間の停学処分中だ。

note.ja: sus（下に）+ pend（吊るす）。下に吊るす →「吊るす・一時停止する・停学にする」。

en: Thin, woven, gauzelike fabric.
A fine transparent silk material, used for veils, etc.; specifically, cloth interwoven with gold or silver threads, or embossed with figu…
To form tissue of; to interweave.
To have the contents of an injection or intravenous drip leak into the tissue as a result of a ruptured or punctured vein.

tissue.ety: From Middle English tissu, from Old French tissu (“woven”), past participle of tistre (“to weave”), from Latin texō (“to weave”).

ex.en: Hand me those tissues there.
ex.ja: そこのティッシュ取って。

ex.en: Does anyone have a tissue?
ex.ja: 誰かティッシュ持ってない？

ex.en: Give a tissue to Tom.
ex.ja: トムにティッシュをあげて。

en: Someone who or something that trails (follows behind); something that is trailing.
Part of an object which extends some distance beyond the main body of the object.
To load on a trailer or to transport by trailer.

trailer.ety: From trail + -er. The film sense derives from the fact that previews were formerly shown after the main feature, rather than before as is usual today, that is trailing after the main feature.

ex.en: He attached the trailer to his car.
ex.ja: 彼は自動車にトレーラーをつないだ。

ex.en: The trailer goes with the car.
ex.ja: トレーラーがその車についている。

en: Below the ground; below the surface of the Earth.
Hidden, furtive, secretive.
Below the ground.
Secretly.
The regions beneath the surface of the earth, both natural (eg. caves) and man-made (eg. mines).
Synonym of subway: a railway that is under the ground.
To route electricity distribution cables underground.

underground.ety:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₁én
Proto-Indo-European *-tér
Proto-Indo-European *h₁entér
Proto-Indo-European *h₂én
Proto-Indo-European *dʰeh₁-?
Proto-Indo-European *-dʰi
?

Proto-Indo-European *(H)n̥dʰér
Proto-Germanic *under

Middle English under

Proto-West Germanic *grundu
Old English grund
Middle English grounde
Middle English undergrounde
English underground
From Middle English undergrounde (adverb), equivalen

ex.en: There is a shopping district underground.
ex.ja: 地下はショッピング街です。

ex.en: In Britain they call the subway the underground.
ex.ja: イギリスでは「ｓｕｂｗａｙ」を「ｕｎｄｅｒｇｒｏｕｎｄ」という。

ex.en: In the underground, to double-cross any member means sure death.
ex.ja: 地下組織では、仲間を裏切ることは、間違いない死を意味する。

en: Against; in opposition to.
Compared with, as opposed to.
To face in competition
To fight

versus.ety: From Middle English versus, borrowed from Latin versus (“facing”), past participle of vertere (“to turn, change, overthrow, destroy”).

note.ja: ラテン語 versus（〜に向かって）から。vers（向ける）。向かい合って →「〜対〜」。

en: In effect or essence, rather than in fact or reality; also, imitated, simulated.
For practical purposes, though not technically; almost complete, very near.
Preceded by the: that which is imitated or simulated rather than existing in fact or reality; (countable) an instance of this.
That which is simulated in a computer and/or online; virtual reality; (countable) an instance of this; specifically (gambling), a compute…

virtual.ety:
PIE word
